properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/20/2021 to PA GEN ENERGY CO LLC in Grant Twp, Indiana county. 78.88(d) - OPERATING WELLS - MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to immediately notify the Department and take corrective actions to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion, rusting or other signs of equipment deterioration that compromise the integrity of the well.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78.88(d) - OPERATING WELLS - MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to immediately notify the Department and take corrective actions to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion, rusting or other signs of equipment deterioration that compromise the integrity of the well.
Violation ID: 927367
Permit API: 063-31807
Unconventional: No
County: Indiana
Municipality: Grant Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/20/2021
Comments: On 8/20/21 OGI J. Branan conducted a follow up inspection on PGE 37-063-31807 Marjorie C Yanity 1025 OG well. The water in the cellar is below the 11-3/4¿ x 16¿ casing. The gas bubbling is not visible due to the water level being below the top of the 11 ¿ ¾¿ by 16¿ casing annulus at the time of the inspection. Based on gas samples taken by Moody & Associates, and evaluation by ECHELON Applied Geosciences Consulting evaluations and interpretations, the gas is identified as lower Mississippian. ¿The gas in the 11-3/4¿ X 16¿ of the Yanity 1025 is likely associated with Lower Mississippi Formations in this area of the basin, possibly the Burgoon (Big Injun) sands.¿ (ECHELON Applied Geosciences Consulting) The Burgoon sands are approximately 400¿ to 500¿ deep. After reviewing ECHELONs evaluations and interpretations, and PGE 37-063-31807 1025 well completion report. Several coal seams and a couple freshwater aquafers were encountered before the casing seat of the surface string. There are freshwater aquafers noted on the well completion report at 83¿ and 130¿ and coal at 27¿ 83¿ 127¿ 152¿ 155¿ and 338¿. The depth of 11-3/4¿ casing is at 568.6¿, a couple hundred feet below the deepest coal. The report identifies the gas source behind the surface casing and a potential to comingle with the identified water aquifers. The Department is denying PGE any request to vent the gas from the 11-3/4¿ x 16¿ annulus as a permeant repair solution. As per 78.86 PGE is required to submit a plan to remediate the issue and has failed to do so. Also, within 30 days of receiving the inspection report, the Department is requesting any Logs or previous predrill data associated with the well.

Comments: This well was drilled in a forested area off of Point View Road in March 2006. A spill was reported to the Department on 11:03 AM on August 27, 2021. Conditions at the site at the time of inspection indicate that this estimate is reasonable. The released production fluid was under pressure and escaped as a mist. Because the estimated spill volume is greater than 1 bbl, an Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process should be followed.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: OIL & GAS MGMT INC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 2/24/2026
Violation Code: 78.121(B) - WELL REPORTING – PRODUCTION REPORTING – Operator failed to electronically submit production and status report to the Department through its web site.
Violation ID: 8265964
Permit API: 111-20249
Unconventional: No
County: Somerset
Municipality: Addison Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/24/2026
Comments: On 2/24/26 at 9:11 AM, I arrived at the Walker 1616 OG Well to conduct a Routine/Complete Inspection. At the time of the inspection all the valves on the well tree were shut (Photograph #4). The well appears to not be producing based on the valve alignment and absence of chart in the meter box. (Photograph #17) A check of DEP records on 2/24/26 found that the operator had not submitted the Annual Production Report for 2025. Violations 78.121(A) and 78.121(B) are being cited for failure to submit annual production. A check of DEP records on 2/24/26 found that the operator has not submitted the Mechanical Integrity Assessment report for 2025. Violations 78.88(e), 78.88(b)1-4 and 78.88(d) are being cited for failure to submit integrity report. The operators posting is attached to the well tree. (Photograph #1) Using a Bascom Turner 611, calibrated on 2/13/26, no gas was detected around the well tree. (Photographs 6-16). The separators have surface corrosion but no signs of leaks, spills or equipment failure were noticed. No gas was detected around the equipment using the Bascom Turner 611. The production tank appears to be in sound condition, no signs of leaks or damage were found. The production tank is not attached to the production equipment. DEP recommend the tank be removed if it is no longer in use. Attached to the meter box is a former operator's posting. The sticker should be removed since it displays incorrect information as to the operator of the well. (Photograph #17)

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/25/2021
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 908944
Permit API: 015-23612
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wyalusing Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/25/2021
Comments: On 02/25/2021, DEP representative John Ciccone conducted an inspection at Chesapeake Appalachia LLC’s (CALLC) Tanner & Hana location. The drilling of 3 wells commenced on location between the dates of 11/12/2020 – 11/13/2020. Drilling operations subsequently followed, were documented within inspection report # 3127696, and had recently finished. The purpose of this inspection was to document the current status of the site and to inspect the site for any indication of possible releases of regulated substances. I arrived onsite at 1335 hours. At the time of my arrival, there were 3 semi-trucks that were hauling timber matting and what appeared to be plastic corrugated pipe off location. There were an additional 11 vehicles parked around the edge of the pad, but no crew members were identified. The weather was 44 degrees with mostly sunny skies. The pad surface was mostly covered in puddles, as warm temperatures melted snow / ice cover. The containment berm and slopes around the site still had approximately 4 – 6 inches of snow cover present. The 3 newly drilled wells were inspected, and all appeared to have back pressure valves set (photo # 3). There appeared to be a thick and dark fluid within each of the well cellars (photo # 4, 5). The area immediately surrounding the wells appeared to have been recently regraded with crushed stone (photo # 6). Just west of the wells, an oily odor was noted. There appeared to be a containment liner still present on the pad surface, partially buried (photo # 7). Puddles on the pad surface around this area (noted in photo # 15) all appeared to have an oily sheen and oily odor (photo # 9, 10, 11). Black specks were present within most of the puddles, and a concentration of a dark substance was noted within a puddle (photo # 12, 13). Sample # 9544-044 was collected from a puddle along the NW edge of the site where both an oily odor and sheen were noted (photo # 14). The sample was collected for SAC 942 + Al, Br, Li analysis. The release of an unknown quantity of a regulated substance to the pad surface is in violation of CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a). Failure to report the release of an unknown quantity of a regulated substance is in violation of 25 Pa. Code 78a.66(b)1. Violations have been cited against well permit # 015-23612. This release is referred to the DEP’s Bureau of Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields. The department recommends: 1. Dewatering the pad surface. 2. Dewatering the well cellars. 3. Removing the tarp liner noted in photo # 7 I departed the site at 1419 hours.

Comments: On May 18, 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IR 4180049.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, Diversified shall restore the site within 9 months of Well plugging in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S. 3216. The well head is observed in the well cellar.During today's inspection, the following was observed:- E and S plan is on site. The E and S plan has not been updated to depict the stream that runs under the access road. - Plastic matting has been removed from all three locations along the access road and from on site. - Disturbance along the access road is observed in multiple areas which appears to be due to vehicle traffic (Photos 4-8, 11-14). The Department recommends the operator repair the disturbance during site restoration.- Sedimentation observed in previous inspection remains visible along the access road above the culvert outlet (Photo 9). The Department recommends the operator return the sediment to the access road and install E and S BMPs above the culvert to prevent sedimentation to the stream channel. - The stream channel (Photo 10) appears to be dry at this time. - The timber mat bridge at the site entrance appears to have been removed (Photo 15).- CFS on the well site appears to be improperly implemented/maintained in two areas (Photos 16-17). The Department recommends the operator ensure CFS is staked with no more than 10 feet between each stake. - Soil stockpile is osberved to be experiencing some vegetative growth on the back side (Photo 20).- Well cellar is observed and well tag/posting requirements are met on site. - Pump jack remains on site at this time. Violations are being continued for failure to construct the site in accordance with the E and S plan, failure to identify a stream on the E and S plan, failure to implement/maintain E and S BMPs, and accelerated erosion and sedimentation off of the access road. Violations were also continued in IR 4201247 for staining still observed near twp previously observed minor releases of petroleum products and/or brine.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 5/01/2023
Comments: On May 1, 2023, I conducted an inspection of the Proffitt 1 well in Derry Township, Westmoreland County. At the time of inspection, the well appeared to drilled, however the well did not appear to be equipped for production. The production line from the well did not appear to be connected to a production unit or other visual production apparatus. The pump jack did not appeared to be operational. The well tag did not appear to match the correct operator information, however the API number appeared to be correct. I observed a significant amount of fluid emanating from the well. I screened the fluid, which appeared to be consisted with fluid produced by a coal bed methane well. The release did not appear to be negatively impacting near by aquatic life, ie tadpoles. Prior to leaving the location, I contacted Apollo Resources Representative Jesse Colangelo to inform him of the release. I recommended that the Operator take immediate action to correct the condition creating the release. Mr. Colangelo indicated that they would sent someone out to correct the leak. I requested photos of the repair once the release was corrected. Violations are being issued for the failure to properly control production fluid resulting in a release to the ground. The Department requests clarification as to what caused the release, the quantity of fluid released and how this was determined, how long it is believed the release was occurring. Please include the clarification information within the NOV response.

Comments: Bull Run Resources contacted WQSS Brian Ayers to inform him of a release that occurred overnight on April 16, 2025 their Peterson P9 well, located in Pleasant Twp Warren County. I arrived on site and spoke with Sam Harvey from Bull Run. Sam informed me that the cause of the release was a high pressure stuffing box on the well head failed for an unknown reason. The emergency low pressure switch on the well head also did not function as designed. Production fluid was released from the well head and traveled downslope following a series of road ditches and culvert crossings. The release does not appear to have progressed past a power line located just north of the well. Several underflow dams have been constructed in the ditch lines and are working effectively at this time. Absorbent pads are being used at the siphon dams to collect any production fluid accumulating behind them. The quantity of the release is estimated between one half to one barrel. Bull Run was having roll off dumpsters delivered while I was onsite. Impacted soil will be removed and disposed of at an approved facility.Upon completion of the remediation, confirmatory samples are expected to be collected and their results provided to the Department. Documentation verifying the disposal of the impacted soil is also expected to be provided to the Department.

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/24/2025
Comments: On March 24, 2025, the Department conducted a follow up Inspection of the RWS Development 001 Well in response to an incident which is documented in IR 3941481 and 3941519 where violations were issued for a brine release. Present during today's inspection was operator representative Ronald Seich.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed charred vegetation on a slope adjacent to the well site, no erosion or sedimentation issues were observed. A wellhead was observed with a well tag fixed to it with all required information posted on it, and no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this wellhead. All other production equipment was observed removed and loaded/being loaded onto a trailer for disposal.It appeared excavation had been started in the area where the production equipment was removed. Excavated material/soil was observed loaded onto tarps. No excavation appeared to have been started on the ditch. Mr. Seich stated that they planned on having all excavation completed, including the ditch, by the end of the day. He also stated that Moody would be onsite tomorrow (3/25/2022) to perform a site assessment and collect samples to evaluate their remediation.A soil conductivity reading was taken in the area where the production tank was previously located with a reading of 0.34mS. The Department observed standing fluid in the ditch/channel in several locations. Conductivity readings were taken of the fluid in the ditch in several locations with readings of 16.00mS, 9.16mS, 2.30mS, 0.87mS, 0.83mS, and 0.80mS. The conductivity readings appeared to decrease with distance from the well/production tank. No standing fluid was observed in the ditch in approximately the last 45 feet prior to terminating near the stream. There did not appear to be a recent flow path of fluid in the section of ditch from the last location of standing water to the remainder of ditch before the stream. A conductivity reading was taken in this area of the ditch with a reading of 0.34mSA conductivity reading was then taken in the stream in the area where the ditch appears to terminate prior to the stream with a reading of 0.73mS. No sheen, discoloration, or foaming was observed in the stream.Based on the Department's observations and conductivity readings obtained, it appears that the conductivity readings are comparable to the previous inspections in regards to distance and levels of elevated readings in the ditch. It appears that released fluids may have been contained to the portions of the ditch where standing fluid was observed, and it did not appear from the observations and readings that there was a release into Waters of the Commonwealth.Bases on today's inspection, violations remain outstanding.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 860202
Permit API: 117-22055
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Liberty Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-08-28
Comments: I inspected the site in response to a reported spill(Complaint ID#344679). I met Mike Deming of SWN when I arrived. He informed me that after washing and vaccing the liner yesterday, the liner and felt were placed in 4 rolloff containers that Waste Management had sent to the site without interior liners. In the process of loading the liner and felt into the containers, the loader compresses the material with the bucket; soapy water was then observed running out of the end of the rolloffs. Mike believes that the felt retained some rig wash solution (SDS forthcoming) and water, and that the compression of the material squeezed this mix out. He stated that the estimate of 2 barrels (84 gallons) was probably high, but that SWN was committed to an Act 2 cleanup process. The affected area appeared to be approximately 30' x 70'; puddled water on the pad in this area showed consistent conductance readings of 1.21-1.28 mS/cm. Two of the rolloffs were still on the pad with the swing gate end raised up on rig mats; while I was on location, a vac truck was used to suck the water out that had collected in the low end of the rolloffs. The north sed trap (.147 mS/cm) and the south sed trap (.441 mS/cm) appeared to be unaffected by the release. The rolloffs were removed and the free water on the pad was vacced while I was on site; a skid steer was scraping the area when I departed. Moody & Associates employees were directing the excavation with conductance meters, and Mike expects confirmation sampling to occur later today or early tomorrow. The site remediation will be referred to the Department's Environmental Cleanups Program. Violations noted.

Comments: This site is located east off Pine City Road, south of the railroad grade and several hundred yards east of the storage yard. There was a several gallon oil release located at the tank battery for this well west of the storage yard. The oil spill is at the end of the tank discharge pipe on the outer embankment of the secondary containment. WQS Taylor contacted Ben Ochs about this oil release, he stated that he had spilled this oil about a week ago and was planning to clean it up. You are hereby requested to follow Department Policy 800-5000-001, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil & Gas Well Sites or Access Road. This Policy sets forth the procedures that should be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release noted in this Notice of Violation by using the Small Spill Cleanup Process, which states: For spills of less than 42 gallons at a well site that do not pollute waters of the Commonwealth or threaten pollution of these waters, the responsible party should remove the soil visibly impacted by the spill upon discovery of the spill and should dispose of the impacted soil by a method permitted by law. The responsible party should notify the Department of its intent to remediate a spill in this manner at the time notification of the spill is made.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/04/2023
Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted after the operator reported a release of produced fluid to the surface of Pad A from GPU #3 on 9/18/23. An area between GPU #3 and the southwest pad edge has been excavated including in the stormwater channel at the pad edge. Some fluid was present in the channel which had an electrical conductivity (EC) of 910 uS/cm. On Pad A, an area of secondary containment has been set up for the excavated pad material. The material has been tarped. The containment appears to be in good condition.Six wells are staged for production on Pad A. Six GPUs are present and appear to be in good condition.On Pad B, nine wells are staged for production. Nine GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs and containment appear to be in good condition. Multiple batteries of frac tanks are present on the pad within secondary containment. A few puddles of fluid are present on the pad surface in front of the frac tank batteries which had an EC between 2.40 to 2.50 mS/cm. The Department recommends vacuuming up the fluid. The EC of the fluid in the sump at the east end of the north stormwater channel has an EC of 1645 uS/cm.Along the access road, vegetation has germinated where excavation took place after a truck rollover caused a release of produced fluid to an area surrounding the access road. The area is not yet permanently stabilized. Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21855 for release of produced fluid to the surface of Pad A from 9/18/23.Violations remain outstanding for the release to Pad B from 12/19/22.

Permit API: 039-24590
Unconventional: No
County: Crawford
Municipality: Hayfield Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/08/2021
Comments: Onsite for an incident response to a reported release from the operator. The release was reported at 2:05pm on Monday, 6/7/2021. The release to the ground occurred as a result of the 4 1/2" casing pressuring up during routine maintenance on the well with a service rig. The 2" tubing was blown down prior to the incident. The estimated volume of oil released to the ground is 30 gallons. Consisting of pooled oil and misted oil around the rig and wellhead and spreading out within the hay field approximately 65-80 feet from the well. Approximately 19 gallons of pooled oil was collected and placed into the production tank. The vegetation (hay) that was covered with the mist of oil was cut down and bagged up for disposal. The majority of the impacted area was scrapped up with an excavator and loaded into a triaxle truck for disposal. Clean fill onsite was being applied to the excavated area as part of the cleanup/reclamation. The cleanup operation will continue Violations cite.

Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess site conditions after a reported release of produced fluid on Pad A in November of 2021. Both pads and the access road were snow-covered during this inspection. On pad A, six wells are staged for production. Six GPUs are present within secondary containment and they appear to be in good condition. The area that had been excavated after the November release appears to have been backfilled. The contaminated material has been removed from the site. Preparations are underway for the frac on Pad B. I met with EQT representative Rick Hall upon my arrival on Pad B. According to Mr. Hall, the excavated area on Pad A has been backfilled with the available topsoil on the site. Additional topsoil will be hauled in to finish the restoration of the excavated area, Mr. Hall said. No issues noted. Violations remain outstanding from the November 2021 release on Pad A.
